title: Enterprise onboarding HC & price-trigger scan Q4 2026
body:
SUMMARY:
This sheet models the incremental headcount, cash burn, and pricing sensitivity for a dedicated Enterprise Onboarding offering (fixed fee + per-seat). Purpose: validate price trigger bands for prioritizing hires and run-rate targets that preserve gross margin >= 45% under shallow adoption scenarios.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS:
- Offering: 1x fixed onboarding fee (one-time) + monthly per-seat charge. Typical deal size for target customers: 100-2,000 seats.
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jan-Dec 2027 planning window used for phasing).
- Burden multiplier (salary+taxes+benefits+ops): 1.35. Contractor cost assumed at 1.6x base rate.
- Estimated conversion at current pricing: baseline conversion rate for trials -> paid 18% (enterprise leads funnel). Elasticity estimates: every -10% price -> +8% conversion; every +10% price -> -6% conversion.
- Onboarding delivery mix: 40% SE-led live sessions, 40% implementation engineering, 20% PM/CS oversight.

HEADCOUNT PLAN (new hires incremental to baseline) - planned hires across Q1/Q2 2027:
Role,New FTEs,Avg salary,Monthly burdened cost
Solutions Engineer,3,$160,000,$18,000
Implementation Engineer,2,$150,000,$16,875
Customer Success (Onboard),2,$130,000,$14,625
Onboarding PM,1,$170,000,$19,125
Sales Engineer (pre-sales support),1,$155,000,$17,431
Contractor (temp trainers),2,$90/hr (est),$15,000 (monthly total)
Notes: monthly burdened cost = salary / 12 * 1.35 (rounded). Contractor row is total cost estimate for cohorts.

MONTHLY CASH BURN MODEL (first 6 months shown as excerpt) - staffing + one-time infrastructure/procurement:
Month,Headcount payroll,Contractors,Tools/cloud,One-time infra,Total monthly burn
Jan-2027,$100,056,$15,000,$7,500,$25,000,$147,556
Feb-2027,$123,687,$15,000,$7,500,$0,$146,187
Mar-2027,$123,687,$15,000,$7,500,$0,$146,187

Assumptions: ramp hires onboarded across Feb-April; one-time infra (training environment, demo license, hardware staging) in Jan = $25k.

REVENUE & PRICING SENSITIVITY (model):
- Baseline pricing: $20k fixed onboarding fee + $0.15/seat/month (example enterprise SKU).
- Baseline adoption assumptions: average seats per closed deal = 450, average deal length = 18 months, expected closed deals in year 1 = 18 (with hires).

Scenarios computed (12-month run-rate revenue contribution + gross margin est):
Scenario A - Baseline:
  Closed deals: 18, Avg seats: 450
  One-time onboarding rev = 18 * $20,000 = $360,000
  Monthly seat rev = 18 * 450 * $0.15 = $1,215/month -> annualized (12mo) $14,580
  Note: monthly seat rev small in this product example (we use higher seat count in run-rate triggers below).

Scenario B - Price -20% (to test uptake)
  Price effect: fixed fee -> $16k, seat -> $0.12
  Elasticity assumption: +16% closed deals -> 20.9 deals (round to 21)
  One-time rev = 21 * $16,000 = $336,000
  Monthly seat rev = 21 * 450 * $0.12 = $1,134/month -> annualized $13,608
  Commentary: lower price increases deals but reduces immediate landed cash/seat. Need to evaluate gross margin.

Scenario C - Price +15% (premium packaging)
  Price effect: fixed fee $23k, seat $0.1725
  Elasticity assumption: -9% closed deals -> ~16.4 deals (round to 16)
  One-time rev = 16 * $23,000 = $368,000
  Monthly seat rev = 16 * 450 * $0.1725 = $1,242/month -> annualized $14,904
  Commentary: more cash per deal but fewer deals. Evaluate ARR growth vs. unit economics.

SENSITIVITY TABLE (what moves gross margin below 45%):
Levers tested: higher contractor days, slower conversion, increased cloud demo costs, reduced seat counts per deal.
- Base gross margin with baseline hiring and costs = 52% (onboarding product line isolated).
- If conversion drops 25% (from 18% -> 13.5%) without offsetting price change -> gross margin falls to ~39% (breach).
- If contractor costs double during ramp -> margin falls to ~44% (close to threshold).
- If seats per deal drop to 300 avg -> margin ~41%.

BREAKEVEN PRICE CALC (simplified):
- Target gross margin threshold: 45%
- Using baseline staffing & cost per closed deal (estimated delivery hours translated to cost): required fixed onboarding fee to hit 45% with 18 deals and 450 seats = $18,400 (baseline $20k is safe).
- If seats per deal fall to 300, required fee -> $24,200.

RECOMMENDATIONS / PRICE TRIGGER LOGIC:
1) Green (no hire pause): if conversion >= 14% and avg seats/deal >= 400 AND contractor spend <= plan -> proceed to hire all planned FTEs.
2) Amber (stagger hires): if conversion between 10-14% OR seats/deal 300-400 -> delay second wave of hires (hold 2 FTEs) and push more contractor support for 3 months.
3) Red (pause hires): if conversion < 10% OR gross margin forecast < 42% with current bookings -> freeze hires, increase price or tighten scope (deliver fewer deliverables per deal) to restore unit economics.

ACTION ITEMS:
- Finance: bake this tab into the master FY27 staffing model and add sensitivity toggles for conversion and avg seats (owner: Miguel Rivera; due: 2026-11-20).
- Sales Ops: add an opportunity field for "expected seats" and require it in the sales checklist to improve forecast quality (owner: Lena Chen; due: 2026-11-30).
- Product: produce a reduced-scope onboarding SKU (50% deliverables, lower price) as fallback for price-sensitivity Red case (owner: Tomás Alvarez; due: 2027-01-15).

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS (working doc style):
- Are we double-counting any seat revenue elsewhere in the product catalog? Confirm with revenue ops.
- Elasticity numbers are from historical small-sample pilot (n=12). Need a larger A/B experiment in Q1 to refine elasticity.
- Consider bundling onboarding into Dedicated contracts as discount lever; requires legal SOW template update.

VERSIONING / CHANGES SINCE LAST PASSES:
- 2026-11-02: initial draft (Asha)
- 2026-11-07: added contractor row and infra one-time item (Miguel)
- 2026-11-12: adjusted elasticity assumptions after pilot review (Lena)
- 2026-11-15: converted to in_review and added action owners (Asha)

Attachments (suggested uploads): cost breakdown CSV, hire phasing GANTT (sheet), pilot elasticity raw data (sheet).

End of sheet excerpt.
